stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: For decades, relief printmakers have cleaned ink from their carved blocks with mineral spirits, a solvent that removes oil-based ink quickly. Printmaker Ana Ruiz, however, now tells students in her workshops to use vegetable oil followed by soap and water. She notes that fumes from mineral spirits can linger for hours in small studios with little ventilation. Ruiz's recommendation suggests that, in her view, ______
choices: vegetable oil leaves behind stronger and longer-lasting fumes than mineral spirits do.
mineral spirits have a drawback in some studios that the oil-and-soap method avoids.
mineral spirits should be banned from every printmaking studio regardless of its size.
students should give up relief printing in favor of techniques that use no ink at all.
explanation: Ruiz recommends a new cleaning method and gives one reason: mineral spirit fumes linger in small, poorly ventilated studios. To recommend the switch for that reason, she has to believe that mineral spirits have this drawback in some settings and that the oil-and-soap method avoids it. That is the smallest belief her advice depends on.

A.why: This reverses the comparison. Ruiz recommends vegetable oil because mineral spirits cause the fume problem, so she can't think the oil gives off worse fumes.

C.why: You took the claim too far. Ruiz says the problem is fumes in small studios with poor ventilation. That gives no support for banning the solvent everywhere, including large, well-ventilated studios.

D.why: Ruiz's advice is about how to clean blocks, not whether to keep printing. Nothing in the text suggests she wants students to stop using ink.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Vaccination rates in Corley County have long been lowest in rural townships, many of which are more than an hour's drive from the nearest clinic. Last spring, the county health department began sending mobile vaccination vans to those townships on a weekly schedule rather than adding staff to its existing clinics. The department's decision suggests that it believed ______
choices: residents near the clinics needed the vans more urgently than rural residents did.
the existing clinics should be closed and replaced entirely by mobile vans.
distance from clinics was keeping some rural residents from getting vaccinated.
vaccines given inside a vehicle work better than vaccines given in a clinic.
explanation: The department sent vans to the far-off townships with low vaccination rates instead of adding staff to the clinics. That only makes sense if it believed the distance to a clinic was part of the problem, and that bringing vaccines closer would reach people the clinics were missing.

A.why: This reverses who the vans are for. The department sent them to the distant townships, not to residents who already live near clinics.

B.why: Adding vans for distant areas doesn't mean the department thinks the clinics are useless. Nothing suggests it plans to close them, so this belief goes beyond anything the action requires.

D.why: The vans solve a problem of access, not effectiveness. The department's action doesn't depend on any belief about where vaccines work best.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Many dialect surveys rely on formal interviews in which participants read lists of words aloud to a researcher. Linguist Tomas Rehn took a different approach, recording participants as they chatted with relatives over meals at home. Rehn pointed out that people often adjust their pronunciation when they know their speech is being studied. Rehn's approach suggests that, in Rehn's view, ______
choices: reading word lists aloud captures everyday speech better than casual conversation does.
formal interviews produce no data of any value to researchers studying dialects.
relatives at mealtimes usually speak a different language than the participants do.
formal word-list readings may not fully reflect how people ordinarily speak.
explanation: Rehn chose casual home recordings over formal word lists and noted that people change how they speak when they know they're being studied. That choice depends on the belief that formal readings may not fully show everyday speech. It's a limited claim, which is the kind the text supports.

A.why: This reverses the comparison. Rehn moved away from word lists because they may distort natural speech, so Rehn can't think they capture everyday speech better.

B.why: You pushed 'limited' all the way to 'worthless.' Rehn only needs to think formal interviews miss something about ordinary speech, not that they have no value at all.

C.why: The relatives are just part of the setting. The text never suggests they speak another language, and Rehn's method doesn't depend on that.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Early studies of minimum-wage laws often compared employment in states that raised their minimum wage with employment in states that did not. Economist Priya Nandakumar instead compared pairs of neighboring counties on opposite sides of a state border, observing that whole states differ in climate, industry, and population in ways that also affect hiring. Nandakumar's research design suggests that she thought ______
choices: comparing whole states can mix the effects of wage laws with other differences.
neighboring counties differ from each other more than entire states usually do.
minimum-wage laws have no effect at all on employment in any part of a state.
county governments, rather than states, usually set minimum-wage levels.
explanation: Nandakumar switched to comparing neighboring counties because whole states differ in many ways that also affect hiring. Her design depends on the belief that state-to-state comparisons can blend the effect of wage laws with those other differences. Neighboring counties are more alike, so they separate the two more cleanly.

B.why: This reverses the comparison. Nandakumar compares neighboring counties because they're more alike than whole states, not less.

C.why: Her design is a way to measure what wage laws do. It doesn't assume they do nothing, and the text gives no sign of what she found.

D.why: The text says states raised their minimum wages. Nandakumar uses counties to make the comparison, not because counties set the wage.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Many shop owners in downtown Arvale assume that their customers mostly arrive by car. Yet when city planners converted a dozen downtown parking spaces into small seating areas, they cited a survey showing that most downtown shoppers walk or take the bus. The planners went ahead despite merchants' warnings that sales would fall. The planners' decision suggests that, in their view, ______
choices: most downtown shoppers depend on finding a parking space close to the stores.
every parking space downtown should be turned into seating as soon as possible.
bus routes into downtown should be extended farther out into the suburbs.
losing a few parking spaces would not greatly reduce the number of shoppers.
explanation: The planners removed parking even though merchants warned sales would fall, and they pointed to a survey showing that most shoppers walk or take the bus. Acting on that evidence only makes sense if they believed that losing a dozen spaces wouldn't drive away many shoppers.

A.why: This is the merchants' view, and the planners' survey undercuts it. You gave the planners the opinion they argued against.

B.why: The planners converted a dozen spaces. That doesn't mean they want to remove all downtown parking, and nothing in the text supports that larger claim.

C.why: Buses come up only as evidence of how shoppers get downtown. The planners' decision says nothing about extending bus service.
